content.text:
**Migration report**

Four interaction-style features were tried, and none was convincing. The strongest t-statistic was only about one in magnitude.

The clearest failure was the wage-change and hours-change rank interaction. Its mean information coefficient was slightly negative, at about -0.02, with a t-statistic near -1, and it showed no difference across regimes of the common index.

The separation-rate versus hiring-rate spread, restricted to the high regime of the common index, gave a small positive coefficient. That was the opposite of the predicted sign, and the feature was undefined in the low regime. Coverage fell to 0.82.

The history-standardized separation-rate feature had very low coverage, about 0.54, and produced weak results.

Next I would try simpler, higher-coverage features and check their signs.
